reason: The packet proves the corrected local structural conclusion: under unique-MST hypotheses a tied minimum cut crosser cannot lie outside T, using the strict fundamental-cycle maximum and a cheaper crossing edge contradiction. This repairs the asserted exchange premise, without claiming to repair the false target theorem.
A bridgeless triangle explicitly replaces an input graph that is itself a tree; this removes the named degeneracy.

Every supplied input still repeats values. Having three distinct values does not remove equality or tied-value degeneracy, and the packet provides no all-distinct instance or perturbation argument. Its claim that the witness is not an artifact of equal values alone is not supported by removal of that named restriction.

The packet states that delta(S) is a bond when G, G[S], and G[T] are connected and reports bounded zero-failure checks. It does not explain why the proposed cut is minimal under that condition; calling it a true theorem is not the required repair argument.
The headline explicitly requires G connected, and the displayed C4 witness satisfies that restriction while the local cut claim fails.

The packet gives only an only-if path criterion. Its component explanation makes a sufficient local repair readily derivable, but does not explicitly state or demonstrate that direction. Under the strict full-argument rule the flag should be reconsidered.
The packet explicitly extends the same failing exchange to the MST setting by assigning unit weights and explaining why both trees are MSTs.
The exact decomposition of P into a segment plus its recession cone yields the corrected finite-supremum sign condition and max(c1,c2); the full packet explains the formula.
The packet describes scanning all disjuncts, explains the no-complementary-pair test and its two-pointer logarithmic-space implementation, and connects the test to satisfiability.
The weaker corrected claim S<=OPT is explicitly justified because each recurrence branch constructs a valid assignment. It repairs the equality locally without solving the assignment problem.
The single-root corruption construction is parameterized by arbitrary tree size n and the packet derives p=1/(2n-1), E=n, and an unbounded violation ratio.
The explanation identifies the per-leaf contribution of at most one, so allowing only p*n corrupted leaves gives the corrected additive bound. The bounded control is supplementary.
The packet explicitly removes balanced-tree shape as a restriction through all tree shapes in the specified finite range; this is documented shape robustness, not asymptotic robustness.
The packet quantifies over every k>=1 and argues that every spanning-tree outcome on k+1 vertices has k edges, contradicting k-1. This supplies an unbounded graph-size family of failing outcomes.
The corrected edge accounting |E(G)|=|E(G')|+m=k+m is explicitly derived from the spanning-tree edge count.

The full packet supplies the corrected local upper bound 0<=|E(G)|<=1 and explains that the failed step converts a maximum into an attained value. It also identifies complete graphs as the scope where equality is justified.
The absorption identity and cancellation of a positive binomial coefficient explicitly derive the corrected implication 1<=50.
The packet gives arrangements in general position, explicitly excluding parallel lines and triple concurrency, and explains that these witnesses also attain the optimal bounded-region count.

The packet explains the different population weights, but the proposed general uncorrelated-size repair is only supported by an equal-size bounded control. The cited only-if monotonicity sentence is not a sufficient-hypothesis proof; a full derivation of the claimed repair is absent.
An explicit interior-probability, static-size mixture replaces the separately identified p=1/n=1 degenerate mixture. The rational expectations are derived, so the named boundary removal is supported.
The full packet proves by induction that every interior pair m>=2,n>=1 is unreachable, using the two-premise requirements and unavailable interior seed. It explicitly treats the unbounded closure.

The packet explains that each step needs two adjacent known lines and that the existing base set supplies only one in each direction. Adding the full m=2 or n=1 base line supplies the missing seed, explaining the stated repair.

For every k>=5 the explicitly parameterized listed entry has 2k+1 rather than k elements, with a displayed counting derivation. This is an infinite family refuting the validity of the displayed entry, not an independently justified claim about all unseen classification entries.

The corrected endpoint is proposed and its doubling cardinality is asserted, but the packet does not derive the sumset for all k>=5. The finite k checks and cardinality calculation alone do not justify the full repaired classification entry.
For r=1 and every even n>=6 the packet explicitly derives LHS-RHS=n-4>0, proving the infinite family.
The primary witness explicitly survives integer-valued 5n/2, positive r, and the residual-size requirement 3r<=n.
With b a fixed unit, every a is coprime to b; the norm-minimality argument excludes every a except alpha*b. In the specified infinite quadratic rings this is an unbounded discrete family.
The packet supplies explicit nonunit a,b examples with Bezout identities and failed norm inequalities, removing the named unit case.
Every nonzero real t gives L(t,0)=(t,t) outside y=-x. The packet proves both the image formula and the unique intersection at the origin.
Substitution of the entire x-axis parameterization explicitly yields the corrected image y=x.
The packet quantifies over every negative integer a and nonzero integer polynomial g, and uses nonnegative content versus strictly negative a*cont(g) to prove failure.

The sign argument proves the old formula false, and the packet states the absolute-value correction and checks it on a bounded sample. It does not explicitly derive gcd scaling or the primitive-factor argument needed to prove the correction generally.
The packet derives an impossible multiplier equality (d+2)(d-1)=1 for all integers d>=2 in the explicitly positive-binomial domain, covering an unbounded family.
The source gives the correct binomial corollary and explicitly rearranges it by division through r-j-1; the nondegenerate range ensures this denominator is nonzero.
The explicit r=2,j=0 example keeps both binomial coefficients within range and strictly positive, removing the named zero/out-of-range cases.
The degree argument applies uniformly to the stated odd positive integer n: every term has degree n while the proposed monomial has degree 2n, so the two cannot agree.
The packet derives the corrected conjugation order by left-multiplication and the coset membership criterion.
The original equations dem=a and den=b provide explicit integer divisibility witnesses for the corrected common-divisor statement; the explanation reverses the faulty divisibility direction.

The packet replaces the false numerical estimate with the exact factorization and evaluates the corrected coefficient. This fixes the quoted local expression, although it does not supply a uniform coefficient for the complete continuity proof.

The packet states the general corrected restriction to im(G), but proves it only for the displayed embedding/projection example. It does not give the general injectivity argument for the repaired universally quantified statement.
